note_tweet.text:
Most of what I give my bots is tasks. Check this inbox. Pull these results. Draft that post.

One evening I tried something different. I gave them my actual goal.

Not "build a website." The long one. Someday living off our own family's ideas and products. Above all, something online that needs very little of my time once it runs.

So I opened a separate group chat for it, with just two bots in it: my personal advisor bot and the one that was then on trial as a startup builder. That room had one topic. The online tutor idea. Nothing else allowed in.

It felt a bit silly typing a life goal into a chat with two AIs. Like telling your coffee machine about your five-year plan.

Then I realized why it mattered. Every task I give them now has a direction. When a bot suggests something that eats more of my evenings, it's off course, and they can see that too.

The family business stays what it is: a school of entrepreneurship for my sons. The tutor is the long game.

My Grok Bot team knows the destination now. I still have to drive.

Have you ever told your tools the "why" and not just the "what"?

#GrokBot #indiehackers
